definitions.explanation: The larval stage of moths and butterflies, especially those covered with hair or bristles. Some species can cause skin irritation.

examples.english: There was a caterpillar on the tree leaves.

examples.japanese: {毛虫|けむし}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{触|さわ}ると→触る：00808_sawaru⟧⟦{痒|かゆ}く→かゆい：02340_kayui⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧⟦こと→こと：01164_koto⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦あります→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: Touching caterpillars can sometimes make you itchy.
Caterpillars turn into butterflies or moths.

examples.japanese: ⟦{春|はる}→春：00627_haru⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なると→なる：01970_naru⟧{毛虫|けむし}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{多|おお}く→多い：01127_ooi⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: Caterpillars become more common in spring.

examples.japanese: ⟦{子|こ}ども→子供：00554_kodomo⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{毛虫|けむし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}つけて→見つける：01180_mitsukeru⟧⟦{怖|こわ}がっていた→怖がる：07574_kowagaru⟧。
examples.english: The child found a caterpillar and was scared.

notes:
{毛虫|けむし} refers specifically to hairy caterpillars.

⟦{毛|け}→毛：01392_ke⟧ means "hair" and ⟦{虫|むし}→虫：02262_mushi⟧ means "insect/bug."

Note: Smooth caterpillars without hair are called ⟦{芋虫|いもむし}→芋虫：13965_imomushi⟧ (literally "potato bug").

Caution: Some {毛虫|けむし} have urticating (stinging) hairs that can cause skin irritation or allergic reactions. The ⟦{茶毒蛾|ちゃどくが}→茶毒蛾：noentry⟧ (tea tussock moth) caterpillar is particularly known for this in Japan.
